title: Chapter 1: The first dead tree
licence: Original sample written for this project
text: On the first morning of autumn, Ines Varga found that one of the glass trees in the upper orchard had gone dark. The glass trees of Halden gave off warmth through the winter, and the village had no other way to keep its fields from freezing. Ines was the youngest of the orchard wardens and had been given the upper rows to watch only a month before. She laid her palm against the dark trunk and found it as cold as river stone. A crack ran from the root to the lowest branch, and a grey powder had gathered inside it. Ines scraped some of the powder into a twist of paper and ran down the hill to the warden house. Head Warden Oskar Brandt refused to be alarmed. He said old trees sometimes died and told her to say nothing, because the harvest fair was in three days and frightened people would sell their land to the lowland merchants. Ines did not agree, but she promised to stay silent until the fair was over. That evening she took the twist of paper to Mother Sabela, an old glassblower who had tended the orchard before Oskar became head warden. Sabela rubbed the powder between her fingers and tasted it. She said it was salt, and that no salt should ever be found in the upper orchard. Sabela then told Ines that the trees drank from a spring under the hill, and that someone or something had fouled it. She warned Ines that if one tree had gone dark, its neighbours would follow before the first hard frost.
